meta.name: RPSGT Limb Movement Visual Pack 1
meta.sourceBasis: Built from the uploaded Sleep Pathways Guild polysomnography reference plus current public AASM ISR limb-movement scoring help. No patient tracing or proprietary scoring-manual figure is reproduced.
meta.clinicalBoundary: Educational scoring-pattern practice only. Current official AASM guidance, facility policy, and supervised scorer competency remain authoritative.

cases.title: N2 series with closely paired bilateral movement
cases.rationale: This teaching segment contains four movement events after the closely paired bilateral bursts are treated as one movement. The onset-to-onset spacing remains within the public AASM ISR series window. Some movements are followed by EEG arousal activity, which is useful context but does not create the series by itself.

evidence.answer: Four movement events remain after the closely paired bilateral bursts are treated as one movement; their onsets remain within the series interval.
options: Four movement events remain after the closely paired bilateral bursts are treated as one movement; their onsets remain within the series interval.
Five separate movements must be counted because each leg channel is always scored independently.
The EEG arousals alone make the leg movements periodic.
The movements occur during wake and therefore cannot be scored.
evidence.rationale: Public AASM ISR help describes at least four movements in a series, 5–90 seconds between movement onsets, and closely paired bilateral movements as one movement unless separated by at least 5 seconds.

cases.title: Three isolated candidate movements in N2
cases.answer: Too few movements for a PLM series
cases.rationale: The movements are individually visible, but there are only three candidate movement events in this teaching window. Public AASM ISR help requires at least four movements for a PLM series.

evidence.answer: Only three candidate leg movements are present, so the minimum series count is not reached.
options: Only three candidate leg movements are present, so the minimum series count is not reached.
Any single leg movement during sleep automatically creates a PLM series.
The movements are too far apart because every PLM must occur less than 5 seconds after the prior movement.
The movements are respiratory-associated and therefore excluded.
evidence.rationale: The important distinction is individual candidate movement versus a qualifying series. A visible leg EMG burst is not automatically a PLM series.

cases.title: Leg movements linked to respiratory-event recovery
cases.answer: Respiratory-associated movements — exclude from PLM scoring
cases.rationale: Each teaching leg movement occurs at the end of, or immediately after, a respiratory event. Current public AASM ISR help says not to score limb movements during a respiratory event or within 0.5 seconds before or after one.

evidence.answer: Each leg movement falls during or within 0.5 seconds of a respiratory-event boundary.
options: Each leg movement falls during or within 0.5 seconds of a respiratory-event boundary.
The movements must be PLMs because their onsets are roughly 25 seconds apart.
The SpO₂ channel alone determines whether a leg movement is periodic.
Respiratory events never affect limb-movement scoring.
evidence.rationale: The apparent periodic timing is not enough. The respiratory relationship changes whether these movements are scored as periodic limb movements.

cases.title: Periodic-looking leg movements during wake
cases.answer: Wake leg movements — do not score as PLMs
cases.rationale: The leg movements look repetitive, but the teaching segment is wake. Current public AASM ISR help says not to score limb movements during stage W.

evidence.answer: The stage context is wake, so these leg movements are not scored as PLMs even though they look periodic.
options: The stage context is wake, so these leg movements are not scored as PLMs even though they look periodic.
Four movements always create a PLM series regardless of stage.
The absence of a desaturation proves the movements are PLMs.
The movements should be scored only because they alternate legs.
evidence.rationale: Stage context matters. Repetitive wake leg activity may still be clinically or technically important to document, but it is not scored as PLMs under the public ISR rule.
